item.title: Anthropic options could begin trading Monday as investors brace for volatility
item.description: Options related to Anthropic shares could start trading shortly after the company completes its initial public offering. Investors are likely to show significant interest in these options due to heightened demand and volatility. The initial public offering is expected to create a wave of trading activity in the options market. Demand for the options could surpass that of previous high-profile offerings, indicating strong investor interest.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Options tied to Anthropic shares could begin trading as early as Monday, giving investors another way to bet on the artificial intelligence company amid expectations of strong demand and heightened volatility, Reuters reported.Cboe Global Markets plans to list the contracts two business days after Anthropic shares begin trading, subject to industry readiness.“The Anthropic IPO could be yet another catalyst, bringing a new wave of investors and trading activity to the options market,” Rob Hocking, Cboe’s global head of derivatives, told Reuters. “It’s great to see investor education driving this growth, as more people learn how options let them define their risk. An exciting trend and one we expect to continue.”The Claude developer is expected to price its IPO after Wednesday’s market close, with its shares scheduled to debut on the Nasdaq on Thursday.For live updates on US Markets, click here“We expect significant interest in Anthropic options once they list,” said Garrett DeSimone, head quant at OptionMetrics. “The combination of AI-driven enthusiasm and the lottery-like payoff profile typical of IPOs is likely to draw investors immediately. As one of the most concentrated pure-play exposures to AI, the stock is also likely to be highly volatile.”Ophir Gottlieb, chief executive of Capital Market Laboratories, said that demand for Anthropic options could exceed the interest seen in SpaceX contracts earlier this year. He cited the offering’s oversubscription, its rising valuation and sharp divisions among investors over the outlook for AI stocks.“The AI trade is melting down,” Gottlieb added. “Many feel it is overdone, while many others feel it’s the popping of a bubble. Whenever there are such opposing views in a heated market, we get a lot of option positioning.”Also Read: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, above target range, according to sourcesOptions give investors the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell shares at a predetermined price within a specified period. They can provide a less expensive way to gain exposure to a stock and express views on short-term price swings or longer-term performance.Anthropic’s $64 billion IPO has attracted stronger early institutional demand than SpaceX’s offering, with the order book six times oversubscribed last week, Reuters previously reported.Wall Street firms are preparing for what could be a record market debut by introducing products linked to Anthropic shares, hosting client events and distributing promotional merchandise.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: Fed policymakers focused on inflation risks in October, with some seeing need for bigger rate hike
item.description: Federal Reserve officials noted a greater risk of inflation requiring more action during their October meeting. Although they decided to keep interest rates steady, discussions indicated a potential need for a half-percentage-point increase. Policymakers expressed concerns over persistent inflation that might not ease quickly enough. The forthcoming December meeting could see intense debates on potential rate hikes and policy adjustments.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday. Almost all policymakers agreed that further rate hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes said, while a few said inflation could prove more persistent and require a shift to a more restrictive policy stance than currently expected. A couple of them went further and argued that the Fed might have to resort to a half-percentage-point increase if incoming inflation data were unfavorable, a benchmark met in recent releases that showed prices rising faster than anticipated.For live updates on US Markets, click hereAmong those who supported keeping the policy rate steady in the 3.75%-4.00% range in October, a few ... indicated that they viewed the decision as a close call, and joined a larger group in urging that the Fed be clear that the decision to maintain the target range did not reflect a weakening of the commitment to hit the US central bank's 2% inflation target.At the end of the two-day session, only Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of lifting the policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point.But the debate highlighted a growing sense at the Fed that inflation will not ease enough on its own for the target to be reached quickly enough. Among those supporting a rate-hike pause, the hope is that coming information will make clearer whether inflation can fall without tighter policy.Prices have been increasing at more than a 3% annual rate, and there has been little improvement in recent months.Last month's meeting also set the stage for a potentially intense debate at the December 8-9 session over the need for a larger rate hike, or at least tougher language about the extent and pace of rate hikes to come, an argument laid out by Fed Governor Christopher Waller in comments to CNBC on Wednesday.The Trump administration has argued that elevated inflation is just temporary and the Fed should ignore it.Inflation has been stronger than expected since the Fed's last meeting, and investors anticipate that the central bank will deliver a quarter-percentage-point rate increase at its meeting next month.The October meeting also saw the beginnings of a more detailed discussion about the impact of artificial intelligence, including discussion of the risks of over-investment in the technology as well as the possible benefits it could bring in the form of rising productivity.
